chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskhan, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to him: A man married a woman and touched her (consummated the marriage). He said: 'She is forbidden to his father and his son, and her dowry is obligatory.'

And the joining of two sisters is permissible in marriage and in possession by right (concubinage). Allah the Exalted said: 'And that you join together two sisters.' Thus, by the apparent meaning of the word, joining them is prohibited in all cases, except that which has been excluded by evidence.

key_terms.بِظَاهِرِ اللَّفْظِ: by the apparent meaning of the word

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying two sisters simultaneously in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific prohibition of *Haml al-Bayn al-Ukhtayn* (joining two sisters), noting that consummation renders the wife forbidden to her father and son while establishing her dowry. It further extends this prohibition to include both formal marriage and concubage (*milk al-yamin*), deriving the ruling from the explicit wording of the Quranic verse which prohibits their simultaneous holding.
